title: Apples to Apples? Towards Comparable Crosslingual Language Model Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2608.25089v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Crosslingual evaluation of language models that enables fair comparisons remains a fundamental challenge in multilingual NLP. Existing studies adopt a variety of downstream tasks and intrinsic metrics with different theoretical justifications, yet there has been little empirical investigation into whether these approaches yield meaningful crosslingual conclusions. We systematically examine crosslingual evaluation approaches using controlled monolingual language models trained on parallel data with varying tokenizer vocabulary sizes and model sizes, and further validate our findings on multilingual LLMs. We further discuss challenges in achieving comparable downstream evaluation across languages. Our results show that several widely used normalized metrics introduce crosslinguistic biases rooted in tokenization, encoding, and orthographic differences. translated_title: 苹果与苹果？迈向可比较的跨语言语言模型评估
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.25089v1 公告类型：新 摘要：语言模型的跨语言评估，能够实现公平比较，仍然是多语言自然语言处理中的一个根本性挑战。现有研究采用了各种下游任务和内在指标，这些方法有不同的理论依据，但对于这些方法是否能产生有意义的跨语言结论，目前缺乏实证调查。我们使用在平行数据上训练的受控单语语言模型，并改变分词器词汇量大小和模型大小，系统地检查了跨语言评估方法，并进一步在多语言大语言模型上验证了我们的发现。我们还讨论了在不同语言中实现可比较的下游评估所面临的挑战。我们的结果显示，几种广泛使用的标准化指标引入了源于分词、编码和正字法差异的跨语言偏见。相比之下，基于语义等价句计算的句子级负对数似然性则更为稳健。
tldr: 本文系统研究发现，跨语言评估中常用的标准化指标因分词和编码差异产生偏见，而基于语义等价句的句子级负对数似然性提供更可靠的比较方法。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically finds that commonly used normalized metrics in crosslingual evaluation introduce biases from tokenization and encoding differences, while sentence-level negative log-likelihood over semantically equivalent sentences offers more reliable comparisons.
